      mean = mean(subset_data),

text:
Tutorial 1 ran lm() got slope intercept. tutorial asks: numbers come , optimize?goal simple linear regression summarize relationship two variables — education wages, match rates 401(k) participation — straight line. line fit every data point perfectly. question : line best? OLS answers minimizing sum squared prediction errors. Squaring penalizes large mistakes small ones, produces unique closed-form solution, connects directly variance decomposition inference.error term \(\varepsilon_i\) (written \(u_i\) Tutorial 3 onward, following Wooldridge — denote object) captures everything moves \(Y\) beyond \(X\): unobserved ability, luck, measurement error.picture . point one observation. blue line candidate fit. red segments residuals — vertical gaps data line. OLS chooses line makes squared gaps small possible.
Figure 3.1: OLS minimizes sum squared vertical distances (red segments). slope intercept chosen line achieves smaller total.
study simple linear regression intercept:\[
Y_i = \beta_0 + \beta_1 X_i + \varepsilon_i, \qquad = 1, \ldots, n
\]regularity condition \(\sum_{=1}^n (X_i - \bar{X})^2 > 0\) (.e., \(X_i\) equal).Sample means:\[
\bar{Y} = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{=1}^n Y_i, \qquad \bar{X} = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{=1}^n X_i
\]OLS objective: Minimize sum squared residuals:\[
S(\beta_0, \beta_1) = \sum_{=1}^n \left( Y_i - \beta_0 - \beta_1 X_i \right)^2
\]Definitions:Fitted values: \(\hat{Y}_i = \hat{\beta}_0 + \hat{\beta}_1 X_i\)Residuals: \(\hat{u}_i = Y_i - \hat{Y}_i\)

chapter: 3 Tutorial 2: Simple linear Regression
heading: 3.1.1 Derive the OLS Normal Equations
text:
Differentiate \(S(\beta_0, \beta_1)\) respect \(\beta_0\) \(\beta_1\) set equal zero.First-Order Condition \(\beta_0\):\[
\frac{\partial S}{\partial \beta_0} = -2 \sum_{=1}^n \left( Y_i - \beta_0 - \beta_1 X_i \right) = 0
\]simplifies :\[
\sum_{=1}^n \left( Y_i - \beta_0 - \beta_1 X_i \right) = 0
\]Expanding:\[
\sum_{=1}^n Y_i = n \beta_0 + \beta_1 \sum_{=1}^n X_i
\]Solving \(\beta_0\):\[
\hat{\beta}_0 = \bar{Y} - \hat{\beta}_1 \bar{X}
\]First-Order Condition \(\beta_1\):\[
\frac{\partial S}{\partial \beta_1} = -2 \sum_{=1}^n X_i \left( Y_i - \beta_0 - \beta_1 X_i \right) = 0
\]simplifies :\[
\sum_{=1}^n X_i \left( Y_i - \beta_0 - \beta_1 X_i \right) = 0
\]Derive Slope Centered Form:Substitute \(\beta_0 = \bar{Y} - \beta_1 \bar{X}\) residual expression:\[
Y_i - \beta_0 - \beta_1 X_i = Y_i - (\bar{Y} - \beta_1 \bar{X}) - \beta_1 X_i = (Y_i - \bar{Y}) - \beta_1 (X_i - \bar{X})
\]Minimizing \(\sum_{=1}^n \left[ (Y_i - \bar{Y}) - \beta_1 (X_i - \bar{X}) \right]^2\) respect \(\beta_1\) gives:\[
\sum_{=1}^n (X_i - \bar{X}) \left[ (Y_i - \bar{Y}) - \beta_1 (X_i - \bar{X}) \right] = 0
\]Rearranging:\[
\sum_{=1}^n (X_i - \bar{X})(Y_i - \bar{Y}) = \beta_1 \sum_{=1}^n (X_i - \bar{X})^2
\]OLS Estimators:\[
\boxed{\hat{\beta}_1 = \frac{\sum_{=1}^n (X_i - \bar{X})(Y_i - \bar{Y})}{\sum_{=1}^n (X_i - \bar{X})^2}}
\]\[
\boxed{\hat{\beta}_0 = \bar{Y} - \hat{\beta}_1 \bar{X}}
\]

Step 1: Write fitted value equationFor observation \(\), fitted value :\[
\hat{Y}_i = \hat{\beta}_0 + \hat{\beta}_1 X_i
\]Step 2: Compute mean fitted valuesSum \(\hat{Y}_i\) divide \(n\):\[
\bar{\hat{Y}} = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{=1}^{n} \hat{Y}_i
= \frac{1}{n} \sum_{=1}^{n} \left( \hat{\beta}_0 + \hat{\beta}_1 X_i \right)
\]Step 3: Split summation\[
\bar{\hat{Y}} = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{=1}^{n} \hat{\beta}_0 + \frac{1}{n} \sum_{=1}^{n} \hat{\beta}_1 X_i
\]Since \(\hat{\beta}_0\) \(\hat{\beta}_1\) constants, factor :\[
\bar{\hat{Y}} = \hat{\beta}_0 + \hat{\beta}_1 \frac{1}{n} \sum_{=1}^{n} X_i
= \hat{\beta}_0 + \hat{\beta}_1 \bar{X}
\]Step 4: Substitute \(\hat{\beta}_0\)Recall OLS intercept estimator :\[
\hat{\beta}_0 = \bar{Y} - \hat{\beta}_1 \bar{X}
\]Substituting:\[
\bar{\hat{Y}} = \left( \bar{Y} - \hat{\beta}_1 \bar{X} \right) + \hat{\beta}_1 \bar{X}
\]Step 5: SimplifyThe terms \(-\hat{\beta}_1 \bar{X}\) \(+\hat{\beta}_1 \bar{X}\) cancel :\[
\bar{\hat{Y}} = \bar{Y}
\]Step 6: Geometric interpretationEvaluating fitted line \(X = \bar{X}\):\[
\hat{Y}(\bar{X}) = \hat{\beta}_0 + \hat{\beta}_1 \bar{X} = \bar{Y}
\], \(X\) equals mean, line predicts exactly \(\bar{Y}\).Conclusion: OLS regression line always passes point \((\bar{X}, \bar{Y})\). \(\blacksquare\)

= \mathbb{E}[Y \mid X] - (\beta_0 + \beta_1 X)

text:
1) law iterated expectations:\[
\mathbb{E}[u] = \mathbb{E}\big[\mathbb{E}[u \mid X]\big] = \mathbb{E}[0] = 0
\]2) Start definition:\[

= \mathbb{E}\big[\mathbb{E}[Xu \mid X]\big]
= \mathbb{E}\big[X \cdot \mathbb{E}[u \mid X]\big]
= \mathbb{E}[X \cdot 0] = 0
\]Therefore \(\operatorname{Cov}(X, u) = 0\).Interpretation. population analogues Part results:sample properties hold automatically OLS fit. population properties require zero conditional mean assumption. parallel coincidence — OLS designed sample moment conditions mimic population ones.

chapter: 4 Tutorial 3: Simple OLS — Residuals, Assumptions, Unbiasedness, Variance, and Interpretation
heading: 4.3.1.1 Question
text:
Using known formula OLS slope,\[
\hat\beta_1=\frac{\sum_{=1}^n (X_i-\bar X)(Y_i-\bar Y)}{\sum_{=1}^n (X_i-\bar X)^2},
\]show :\[
\boxed{\hat\beta_1
=
\beta_1
+
\frac{\sum_{=1}^n (X_i-\bar X)u_i}{\sum_{=1}^n (X_i-\bar X)^2}.}
\]

chapter: 4 Tutorial 3: Simple OLS — Residuals, Assumptions, Unbiasedness, Variance, and Interpretation
heading: 4.3.1.2 Solution
text:
Start decomposition:\[
Y_i-\bar Y
=
\beta_1(X_i-\bar X) + (u_i-\bar u),
\]\(\bar Y=\beta_0+\beta_1\bar X+\bar u\).Multiply sides \((X_i-\bar X)\) sum \(\):\[
\sum (X_i-\bar X)(Y_i-\bar Y)
=
\beta_1\sum (X_i-\bar X)^2 + \sum (X_i-\bar X)(u_i-\bar u).
\]\(\sum (X_i-\bar X)\bar u = \bar u\sum (X_i-\bar X)=0\), \[
\sum (X_i-\bar X)(u_i-\bar u)=\sum (X_i-\bar X)u_i.
\]Divide sides \(S_{xx}=\sum (X_i-\bar X)^2\):\[
\hat\beta_1
=
\beta_1 + \frac{\sum (X_i-\bar X)u_i}{S_{xx}}.
\]Hence desired representation holds.

chapter: 4 Tutorial 3: Simple OLS — Residuals, Assumptions, Unbiasedness, Variance, and Interpretation
heading: 4.3.2.2 Solution
text:
C1:\[
\hat\beta_1-\beta_1
=
\frac{1}{S_{xx}}\sum_{=1}^n (X_i-\bar X)u_i,
\qquad
S_{xx}=\sum (X_i-\bar X)^2.
\]Condition \(X=(X_1,\dots,X_n)\). weights \((X_i-\bar X)/S_{xx}\) constants given \(X\), \[
\mathbb{E}[\hat\beta_1-\beta_1\mid X]
=
\frac{1}{S_{xx}}\sum (X_i-\bar X)\,\mathbb{E}[u_i\mid X].
\]..d. sampling \(\mathbb{E}[u_i\mid X_i]=0\), \(\mathbb{E}[u_i\mid X]=0\) \(\). Therefore\[
\mathbb{E}[\hat\beta_1-\beta_1\mid X]=0
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
\boxed{\mathbb{E}[\hat\beta_1\mid X]=\beta_1.}
\]Finally, apply Law Iterated Expectations:\[
\mathbb{E}[\hat\beta_1]
=
\mathbb{E}[\mathbb{E}[\hat\beta_1\mid X]]
=
\mathbb{E}[\beta_1]=\beta_1.
\]

heading: 4.4.2 D2. Conditional variance of the slope

chapter: 4 Tutorial 3: Simple OLS — Residuals, Assumptions, Unbiasedness, Variance, and Interpretation
heading: 4.4.2.1 Question
text:
Using representation Part C,\[
\hat\beta_1-\beta_1
=
\frac{\sum_{=1}^n (X_i-\bar X)u_i}{S_{xx}},
\]show :\[
\boxed{\operatorname{Var}(\hat\beta_1\mid X_1,\dots,X_n)=\frac{\sigma^2}{S_{xx}}.}
\]

chapter: 4 Tutorial 3: Simple OLS — Residuals, Assumptions, Unbiasedness, Variance, and Interpretation
heading: 4.4.2.2 Solution
text:
Condition full regressor sample \(X=(X_1,\dots,X_n)\). \(S_{xx}\) \((X_i-\bar X)\) constants. Compute:\[
\operatorname{Var}(\hat\beta_1\mid X)
=
\operatorname{Var}\left(\frac{1}{S_{xx}}\sum (X_i-\bar X)u_i \Bigm| X\right)
=
\frac{1}{S_{xx}^2}\operatorname{Var}\left(\sum (X_i-\bar X)u_i \Bigm| X\right).
\]Using conditional uncorrelatedness across \(\):\[
\operatorname{Var}\left(\sum (X_i-\bar X)u_i \mid X\right)
=
\sum (X_i-\bar X)^2\operatorname{Var}(u_i\mid X)
=
\sum (X_i-\bar X)^2\sigma^2
=
\sigma^2 S_{xx}.
\]Therefore:\[
\operatorname{Var}(\hat\beta_1\mid X)
=
\frac{1}{S_{xx}^2}(\sigma^2 S_{xx})
=
\boxed{\frac{\sigma^2}{S_{xx}}.}
\]Interpretation. slope precise () noise smaller (\(\sigma^2\) small) /(ii) \(X\) spread (\(S_{xx}\) large).

heading: 4.4.3.1 Question
text:
Show :\[
\boxed{\operatorname{Var}(\hat\beta_0\mid X)
=
\sigma^2\left(\frac{1}{n}+\frac{\bar X^2}{S_{xx}}\right).}
\]

chapter: 4 Tutorial 3: Simple OLS — Residuals, Assumptions, Unbiasedness, Variance, and Interpretation
heading: 4.4.3.2 Solution
text:
Use:
\[
\hat\beta_0 = \bar Y - \hat\beta_1\bar X.
\]model, \(\bar Y = \beta_0+\beta_1\bar X+\bar u\), :\[
\hat\beta_0-\beta_0 = \bar u - (\hat\beta_1-\beta_1)\bar X.
\]Condition \(X\). \(\bar X\) constant, compute:\[
\operatorname{Var}(\hat\beta_0\mid X)
=
\operatorname{Var}(\bar u\mid X)
+ \bar X^2\operatorname{Var}(\hat\beta_1\mid X)
-2\bar X\operatorname{Cov}(\bar u,\hat\beta_1\mid X).
\]classical assumptions, \(\operatorname{Var}(\bar u\mid X)=\sigma^2/n\). Also already \(\operatorname{Var}(\hat\beta_1\mid X)=\sigma^2/S_{xx}\).remains show covariance term zero. Using
\[
\hat\beta_1-\beta_1 = \frac{1}{S_{xx}}\sum (X_i-\bar X)u_i,
\qquad
\bar u = \frac{1}{n}\sum u_i,
\]
covariance proportional :
\[
\operatorname{Cov}\left(\sum u_i,\ \sum (X_i-\bar X)u_i \mid X\right)
=
\sum (X_i-\bar X)\operatorname{Var}(u_i\mid X)
=
\sigma^2 \sum (X_i-\bar X)=0.
\]Hence:
\[
\operatorname{Var}(\hat\beta_0\mid X)
=
\frac{\sigma^2}{n}+\bar X^2\frac{\sigma^2}{S_{xx}}
=
\boxed{\sigma^2\left(\frac{1}{n}+\frac{\bar X^2}{S_{xx}}\right).}
\]

heading: 4.4.5 D5. Estimated variance and standard errors of OLS
text:
Plug \(\hat\sigma^2\):\[
\boxed{\widehat{\operatorname{Var}}(\hat\beta_1\mid X)=\frac{\hat\sigma^2}{S_{xx}}}
\qquad\Rightarrow\qquad
\boxed{\text{s.e.}(\hat\beta_1)=\sqrt{\frac{\hat\sigma^2}{S_{xx}}}}.
\]\[

\qquad\Rightarrow\qquad
\boxed{\text{s.e.}(\hat\beta_0)=\sqrt{\hat\sigma^2\left(\frac{1}{n}+\frac{\bar X^2}{S_{xx}}\right)}}.
\]Interpretation. Standard errors translate sampling variability scale allows inference (confidence intervals t-tests).

heading: 5.1.1 A1. An additional assumption: normality of errors
text:
Narrative idea. Unbiasedness variance formula hold four Gauss-Markov assumptions alone. pin exact shape sampling distribution \(\hat\beta_1\) — therefore build exact tests — need one assumption.Assumption (Normality error term):\[
u_i \mid X \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2)

Since \(TSS = ESS + RSS\):\[

# When beta* = 6: the test statistic Z = beta_hat / 2 ~ N(6/2, 1) = N(3, 1)

cat("True effect:          beta* =", beta_star, "\n")## True effect:          beta* = 6
cat("Signal-to-noise:      delta = beta*/sigma_hat =", delta, "\n")## Signal-to-noise:      delta = beta*/sigma_hat = 3
cat("Distribution of Z:    N(delta, 1) = N(", delta, ", 1)\n")## Distribution of Z:    N(delta, 1) = N( 3 , 1)

heading: 9.1.4.2 Step 2 — Compute power for beta* = 6 analytically
text: Power = \(P(|Z| > 1.96)\) \(Z \sim N(\delta, 1)\). split two tails.
code:
# RIGHT tail: P(Z > 1.96) when Z ~ N(delta, 1)
# Standardise: let W = Z - delta ~ N(0,1), then Z > 1.96 <=> W > 1.96 - delta
right_tail <- 1 - pnorm(z_crit - delta)   # = P(W > z_crit - delta)

# LEFT tail: P(Z < -1.96) when Z ~ N(delta, 1)
# Z < -1.96 <=> W < -1.96 - delta
left_tail  <- pnorm(-z_crit - delta)       # = P(W < -z_crit - delta)

power_beta6 <- right_tail + left_tail

cat("Right tail contribution: P(Z > 1.96) =", round(right_tail, 4), "\n")## Right tail contribution: P(Z > 1.96) = 0.8508
cat("Left  tail contribution: P(Z < -1.96) =", round(left_tail, 4), "\n")## Left  tail contribution: P(Z < -1.96) = 0
cat("Power at beta* = 6:      ", round(power_beta6, 4),
    "-- i.e.", round(power_beta6*100, 1), "%\n")## Power at beta* = 6:       0.8508 -- i.e. 85.1 %

heading: 9.1.4.5 Step 5 — How does sample size move the curve?
code:
# The SE formula from Wooldridge Theorem 2.2:
#   SE(beta_hat) = sigma / sqrt(SST_x)
#
# For x ~ Uniform(0, 10):
#   E[SST_x] = n * Var(x) = n * 10^2/12
#   => SE = sigma_u / sqrt(n * 100/12)
#
# Larger n => smaller SE => larger delta = beta*/SE => higher power

sigma_u <- 4    # error standard deviation
x_range <- 10   # x ~ Uniform(0, x_range)

# For each sample size, recompute the power curve with the appropriate SE
n_values   <- c(20, 50, 200)
power_by_n <- do.call(rbind, lapply(n_values, function(n) {
  se_n      <- sigma_u / sqrt(n * x_range^2 / 12)   # SE for this n
  delta_n   <- beta_grid / se_n
  power_n   <- pnorm(-z_crit - delta_n) + (1 - pnorm(z_crit - delta_n))

  cat("n =", sprintf("%3d", n),
      "  SE(beta_hat) =", round(se_n, 3),
      "  Power at beta*=2:", round(power_n[beta_grid == 2], 3), "\n")

  data.frame(beta = beta_grid, power = power_n, n = as.character(n))
}))## n =  20   SE(beta_hat) = 0.31   Power at beta*=2: 1 
## n =  50   SE(beta_hat) = 0.196   Power at beta*=2: 1 
## n = 200   SE(beta_hat) = 0.098   Power at beta*=2: 1
ggplot(power_by_n, aes(x = beta, y = power, color = n)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.80, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("20"="#cc5500","50"="#2255aa","200"="#2a7a2a"),

  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2)) +

# Fit OLS to one sample and inspect what confint() computes
set.seed(55)
x_ex <- runif(n_obs, 0, 10)
y_ex <- beta0_true + beta1_true * x_ex + rnorm(n_obs, 0, sigma_u)
m_ex <- lm(y_ex ~ x_ex)

# Extract ingredients manually
beta1_hat_ex <- coef(m_ex)["x_ex"]
se_hat_ex    <- summary(m_ex)$coefficients["x_ex", "Std. Error"]
df_ex        <- m_ex$df.residual           # degrees of freedom = n - 2
t_crit_ex    <- qt(0.975, df = df_ex)      # t critical value (not z, because sigma unknown)

lower_manual <- beta1_hat_ex - t_crit_ex * se_hat_ex
upper_manual <- beta1_hat_ex + t_crit_ex * se_hat_ex

cat("Manual construction of the 95% CI:\n")## Manual construction of the 95% CI:
cat("  beta_hat_1 =", round(beta1_hat_ex, 4), "\n")##   beta_hat_1 = 2.8612
cat("  SE(beta_hat_1) =", round(se_hat_ex, 4), "\n")##   SE(beta_hat_1) = 0.2616
cat("  t critical value (df =", df_ex, ") =", round(t_crit_ex, 4), "\n")##   t critical value (df = 28 ) = 2.0484
cat("  Margin of error = t * SE =", round(t_crit_ex * se_hat_ex, 4), "\n")##   Margin of error = t * SE = 0.5359
cat("  CI = [", round(lower_manual, 4), ",", round(upper_manual, 4), "]\n\n")##   CI = [ 2.3254 , 3.3971 ]
# Now compare with confint()
cf_auto <- confint(m_ex, "x_ex", level = 0.95)
cat("confint() result:\n")## confint() result:
cat("  CI = [", round(cf_auto[1], 4), ",", round(cf_auto[2], 4), "]\n")##   CI = [ 2.3254 , 3.3971 ]
cat("They match -- confint() is doing exactly beta_hat +/- t * SE.\n")## They match -- confint() is doing exactly beta_hat +/- t * SE.

text: Now apply formula Exercise 1, Step 3:\[F = \frac{(SSR_r - SSR_{ur})\,/\,q}{SSR_{ur}\,/\,(n - k - 1)}\]\(F\)-statistic tells many times larger fit loss per restriction compared background noise. \(F \approx 1\), fit loss expect random variation alone — evidence \(H_0\). \(F\) much larger 1, fit loss big explained chance. q <- 2    # number of restrictions (beta_3 = 0 AND beta_4 = 0)

heading: 10.2.5 Step 5. Compute the \(p\)-value and make a decision
text: need two R functions \(F\)-distribution. work exactly like pnorm/qnorm Tutorial 7, \(F\)-distribution instead normal:qf(p, df1, df2) answers: “\(F\)-value fraction \(p\) \(F_{df1, df2}\) distribution ?” gives critical value.Example: qf(0.95, df1 = 2, df2 = 494) returns value 95% \(F_{2,494}\) distribution lies . \(F\)-statistic exceeds value, reject \(H_0\) \(\alpha = 0.05\).pf(x, df1, df2, lower.tail = FALSE) answers: “fraction \(F_{df1, df2}\) distribution lies \(x\)?” gives \(p\)-value.Always use lower.tail = FALSE. Without , pf() returns area \(x\), wrong tail. large \(F\) give \(p\)-value near 1 instead near 0.Now make decision — exactly described Exercise 1, Step 5:
code:
alpha  <- 0.05

# Critical value: the 95th percentile of the F(2, 494) distribution
F_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1 = q, df2 = df_ur)

# p-value: probability of observing F >= F_manual under H0
# lower.tail = FALSE gives the UPPER tail probability
p_val  <- pf(F_manual, df1 = q, df2 = df_ur, lower.tail = FALSE)

cat("Critical value (5%):", round(F_crit, 4), "\n")## Critical value (5%): 3.014
cat("p-value:            ", round(p_val, 4), "\n")## p-value:             0.2716
cat("F-statistic:", round(F_manual, 4), "\n")## F-statistic: 1.3069
cat("Critical value:", round(F_crit, 4), "\n\n")## Critical value: 3.014
if (F_manual > F_crit) {
  cat("DECISION: Reject H0 (F =", round(F_manual, 3),
      "> critical value =", round(F_crit, 3), ")\n")
  cat("Since H0 is TRUE in our DGP, this is a Type I error.\n")
  cat("This happens about 5% of the time --- exactly what alpha = 0.05 means.\n")
} else {
  cat("DECISION: Fail to reject H0 (F =", round(F_manual, 3),
      "<= critical value =", round(F_crit, 3), ")\n")
  cat("Correct decision --- H0 is indeed true in our DGP.\n")
  cat("The test correctly concluded that PrevExp does not affect wages.\n")
}## DECISION: Fail to reject H0 (F = 1.307 <= critical value = 3.014 )
## Correct decision --- H0 is indeed true in our DGP.
## The test correctly concluded that PrevExp does not affect wages.
